reasons.plausibility: The Hall-Petch mechanism is generally not effective at 1273 K (0.6-0.7 Tm) because grain boundaries become sources/sinks for vacancies and dislocations, enabling creep and dynamic recovery, so relying on grain boundary strengthening for a 40-60% strength retention improvement is physically unsound.
reasons.testability: The proposed falsification test is clear and directly compares the SPS-processed alloy to the cast baseline under identical conditions, with a well-defined quantitative criterion for failure.
reasons.usefulness: The hypothesis is not useful because it proposes a mechanism (Hall-Petch) that is known to be ineffective at the target temperature, and the main uncertainty about scaling is irrelevant to the fundamental scientific question of high-temperature strength.
